which was the better adaptation the show or the movie lets find out episode 1 okay ive just about had it with all this tribalism between show fans and book fans with the poorly substantiated emotionally charged claims about the show being more accurate than the movies or the movies being more fun than the show its just sniping at your nonpreferred adaptation to puff up the version you like theres little though little actual exploration just arguments so im here to change this and add some substantiation to my emotionally charged claims im going to go through the movie and show sceneepisode by sceneepisode compare to the book and give my thoughts on which was the better adaptation some ground rulesbiases to be made aware of full disclosure my current position before doing this is that i like the book and the rest of the original pjo series but im not a big fan of hoo besides son and i dont like toa magnus chase or cotg kane chronicles is fire though i like the movie better than the show currently importantnot really people are just dumb this is my analysisreasoning as such there is going to be a fair bit of my opinion in it i am not attempting to state that my opinions are fact rather i am trying to make a case for why other people should agree with my opinionsthe conclusions i draw by showing my reasoning and thought process disagree if you like but if youre gonna come here and say thats not fact its just your opinion this is the one disclaimer you get i will no longer be demarcating my opinions vs fact unless i feel it works phrasing wise this is not about nitpicking or needing 100 11 book accuracy these are adaptations adaptations need to change things ill try to judge not just based on did it follow the book but if following the book worked what was the idea behind the changes were they executed well what was gained what was lost since the physical characteristics of the show cast is a highly divisive topic which has a high likelihood of derailing any intelligent conversation in this post or just getting it removed im going to operate under the assumption that it doesnt matter and the show will not lose any points for the bodily appearances of the actors i just wont talk about it its a free pass in the spirit of fairness this will also apply to the movie aging the characters up i feel its a fair balance if you dont too bad make your own post time will be taken into account budget will not yes thats biased towards the movie which has a shorter runtime and a higher comparative budget but runtime is much more quantifiable and easy to compare and break down as a layman i dont know what the budgets were how they were spent or how efficient budget spending is itd be pure speculation that i dont think is worth it i havent seen season 2 of the show so neither it nor the som movie will be taken into account on a related note since hoo came out after the tlt movie neither work will lose any points for going against posttlo canon the show can still get points for taking said canon into consideration though my general rule for when books contradict things is tltrest of pjoposttlo to avoid this post being monstrously long ill break it up using the shows episodes as a baseline because of how things work thatll mean each comparison will cover from the first event in the shows episodei guess from after the last event in the last episode in case of skips if there are any compared to the corresponding book chapters and chunk of the movie order will be book movie show there is no actual scoring and the points are made up onto episode 1 since this post is already gonna be gigantic episode 1 intro through minotaur chapters 14 section 1 introduction book the book leads off with the dont say i didnt warn you disclaimer a fourth wall breaking speech to the reader setting the stage that being a halfblood is something that you could be but dont want to be and that it is very dangerous that it mostly gets you painfully killed and that its only a matter of time until they start hunting you its foreboding it draws you in it directly asks you to put yourself in percys shows it also doesnt say what a halfblood is yet after that it leads into percys introduction the am i a troubled kid line and then onto the mrs dodds incident three months ago thatll be important later but the juice here is that percy is a 12 year old troubled kid and also a halfblood whatever that is either way you dont wanna be him but what if you are him this is also only like a page and a half for reference movie opening credits finish at 100 title card starts to drop at 440 right off the bat its different we start with thunder and lightning then the lightning abruptly stops poseidon walks up from the ocean as a greekarmored giant scares a fisherman because what even is the mist and then shrinks down into a regular dude in a hoodie and walks to the empire state building there he meets zeus and we learn about the missing bolt that the gods have kids that they cant interact with because of zeus and about the deadlinewar very different intro we havent even met percy yet it still draws you in with the idea of what is a halfbloodhow does a child of a god work i dont think i can assess this with how accurate it is the book its a different scene trying to do different things it sets a different tone putting the main conflict of the book front and center rather than the reality of life as a troubled kiddemigod i appreciate how well it expositions several things naturally though using questions and responses to guide watchers into wanting to learn you pose a question the viewer wants to answer it they are now receptive to hearing your exposition we learn that greek gods are real they live in new york and they have kids but cant interact with them also zeus lightning got stolen which is a big nono and he thinks poseidon had his son do it and they gotta give it back before the solstice or war and also war would be super bad because these dudes blast doors apart rather than using doorknobs and even grabbing each others coats gets a magic impact sound effect the whole scene takes about 3 and a half minutes show starts at 005 title card at 045 starts off with percy narrating in a speech similar to the books opening disclaimer its cleaned up a bit and includes less believe the lie your parents told you but its pretty much the same on screen its storming as a figure walks forward hes looking at something its atmospheric but i dont think its focused enough like ive seen the show i know thats percy but it doesnt do anything to show its percy a minor quibble but i dont see how the visuals and the voiceover connect its a pretty good intro it gets the main thrust of what the book didyes i talked about the book including the troubled kid line but thats coming right after the title card i dont think it makes any bad changes but i dont think it makes full use of the visual aspect good delivery from walker at the same time its a 40 second scene how much can you do visually verdict the show followed the book the movie did something different lets see if it pays off section 2 yancy book the book introduces us to mr brunner grover mrs dodds and explains more about how percy is troubled he has dyslexia and adhd his mind sometimes skips a beat hes involved in all this odd dangerous situations he gets blamed for hes already on probation from his sixth school in six years which makes defending grover from bullies hard we get some foreshadowing with the conversation about kronos and we see mr brunner is a kind of mentor to percy but at the same time while hes not overly harsh percy feels he expects too much from him mrs dodds meanwhile is evil and after percys possible water powers push a bully into a fountain she leads him into the museum turns into a monster and tries to kill him he is saved by mr brunner tossing him a pen that is actually a sword and his own instincts reality then gaslights percy about the whole thing also the weather is crazy things progress percys behavior slips and he is uninvited back but not immediately expelled in the other big yancy scene percy goes to ask mr brunner for study help and overhears grover and chiron dropping plot we learn that mrs dodds was real theyre trying to keep percy alive and there is a summer solstice deadline connected to the winter solstice also mr brunner kind of sucks at communicating interestingly in contrast to both adaptations percy does not get riptide yet mr brunner takes it back at the museum movie title card ends 447 percy comes up for aircredits finish 553 museum left at 1455 okay starting off percy sits underwater for a full minute and 15 seconds onscreenand six more offscreen gee i wonder who his parent is jokes on you the movie already brought up that poseidons son was a central figure okay we start off with percy underwater then talking with grover apparently being underwater is the one place he can think they walk through the halls of yancy which is clearly a school for troubled kids a fight breaks out right behind them and the whole place feels claustrophobic and miserable also grover has crutches i like grover having crutches its an easy way to call attention to his leg thing visually we see how mrs dodds is a jerk a nice representation of how percys dyslexia affects him on a side note movie mrs dodds really fits the yeah its easy to think how she could be an ancient greek monster in disguise vibe appearancewise notably the movie does not go directly into the field trip and also yancys not a boarding school here because were going home i guess were pulling in things from later some more percy explaining he has adhd and dyslexia is not well done dialogue i gotta say percys definitely showing the anger and bitterness he has in the book in the little conversation with his mom who is trying to be supportive enter gabe his opening line is just barking woman gabe in the movie is very well done as a scumbag he passiveaggressively makes sally get him a beer slaps her on the ass in a kitchen right in front of percy and then backs percy up against a wall and gets in his face to intimidate him when called out sally and percys behavior adds to it percy our main character is clearly disgusted by gabe sally is less so sure she answers his question of where is my beer literally but she doesnt make a fuss at being talked down to or ass slapped i do like when she tells percy that gabes been good to them in ways he doesnt understand percy responds youre right i dont understand very percy now onto the museum as they walk up the stairs poseidon gives percy a warning through voiceover and is watching him from behind for a few seconds okay so now we really know hes poseidons son and we get the heads up that the museum is gonna be important dont really like the telepathy thing tbh we get mr brunners lesson in the museum which is different instead of foreshadowing kronos as a villain we get exposition about the gods the big three and their rivalry and about demigods i like the framing of percy answering what the proper name for a halfblood is with mrs dodds right behind him waiting to see what he says if you know they know too we find out percys named after perseus and his dyslexia also translates ancient greek the movie does a good job of showing through visuals that grover and mr brunner know more than theyre letting on no bullies present mrs dodds just take percy into a side room and attacks notably shes trying to find where he stashed the lightning bolt after stealing it not just hinting at something he did and trying to kill him i dont really like her kindly one design it feels more harpy than full fury instead of percy killing her mr brunner threatens her off also we aint gaslighting nothing here instead chiron and grover just discuss things right in front of percy still a bit like their conversation in the book but not really mr brunner still cant communicate because this is a pen and grover is instructed to take percy to camp obviously the movie condenses three months at yancy down to two days cutting the end of the term is a necessary change its much harder to pass time quickly in a movie vs a book and a montage isnt really warranted here i guess they could have added the night before and exam scene after the museum but this whole section only took ten minutes would adding that scene be worth it i dont like percy not killing mrs dodds though yeah this is a pen and all but i wanted to see percy kill mrs dodds its an important scene they didnt do it boo show title card ends 055 yancy left at 1210 we start off with the troubled kid introduction i like that its there but i think it loses a slight bit of punch by leaving out he goes to a school for troubled kids first we see a frazzled teacher finding second grade percy on the roof after having seen a pegasus cool way to show those misadventures that got him kicked out nice well sent to someones office its implied by the changing uniforms that hes moving between schools nice touch then we see it happening again where he sees a bronze rhino automaton which upon further inspection is actually an ordinary garbage truck this kind of thing gets him ostracized this i dont like cool way of showing off the mist but it reframes percys troubles in a way that doesnt vibe with me book percy accidentally fires cannons at school buses and drops fieldtrips into shark tanks show percy stares out windows and draws things these are not the same going out onto a building roof top in second grade because you saw something works getting called a loser because you imagined a garbage truck was a mechanical rhino during lunch does not kids have imagination thats just a normal thing especially since hes not getting these from nowhere they match up with stories his mom tells him sidenote ayy minotaur in tightywhiteys on to the museum where we are informed by percys narration that everything is about to change once again this is the big scene mr brunner starts off by saying the gods are not fictional or fantasies hes being metaphorical but still little on the nose so early we get the dyslexia effect again its a good way of showing it it worked in the movie it works here mr brunner doesnt get a big lecture here instead we get a flashback to percy and his mom the percyperseus connection is acknowledged again we get the foreshadowing that not everyone who looks like a hero is a hero and not everyone who looks like a monster is a monster and also that sally named percy after perceus because of what his mom did and because he managed to get a happy ending this is an example of using questions poorly the viewer is set up with the question why do you think shes a monster but doesnt get an answer were asked to consider than not all who look like heroes are heroes with perseus as the focal point but right after we learn percy is named so because perseus got a happy ending this is framed as a good thing so not all heroes are heroes but this one in particular is is the conclusion we draw from here as a nitpick i dont like how happy percy is in all these flashbacks we hear about how awful his life is but we dont see it on his face we get some bullying mrs dodds intro and mr brunner giving percy the pen ill be honest im not really feeling mr brunner here hes still not good at communicating but unlike book chiron who keeps putting his foot in his mouth or movie chiron who is preoccupied with da stakes show chiron just cant be bothered to explain on a sidenote walkers right this is a pen would have gone hard here and they should have used that take on to lunch the show implies that percy also gets bullied and has not stood up to nancy before i dont like this change it takes away from percys temper his frustration the dialogue between grover and percy is okay but feels a bit dense its trying to convey information but i feel this scene would have better served just showing their friendship then we get the nancy push i dont think it was choreographed well they should have used a cut to blacki know i know instead of showing percy fully intentionally force push nancy into the fountain or choose a different angle where its more visible that the water is doing anything mrs dodds starts speaking in voiceover to percy it was bad when poseidon did it its bad here too i do like from a visual perspective her slowly turning into a kindly one especially the jacket to wings transition not a big fan of the hair but whatever i dont like that this is happening out in the open in a crowded space with seemingly nobody seeing it she threatens percy gets him on the ground and then gets impaled by a sword and slowly disintegrates i didnt like when movie percy didnt kill mrs dodds and i dont like this either percy in the books makes a reflexive choice to swing the sword he kills mrs dodds because of his instincts here we dont even know how he killed her or if it was him also the whole scene just feels like its in slow motion theres no tension no urgency people didnt see mrs dodds double leg takedown percy but then the suddenly all notice that percys on the ground and then they do the gaslight but its just mr brunner saying it and we know hes connected via the pen so is he just lying percy gets expelled because grover liessorta about him having pushed nancy i have my feelings on this but i cant fully explain my reasoning as to why they decided to do it until next section so lets just table it for now we get the conversation between percy and mr brunner mr brunner does better this time at feeling like the book version i like the little head nod he does to show he realizes he kinda blew it both the movie and the show spend roughly the same amount of time on this section i dont have any thoughts on that its just kind of cool similarly to the movie the show omits the rest of the term and has percy expelled immediately same reasoning applies there its an easy adaptational change unlike the movie the show follows the same skeleton as the book pretty closely with one difference the show omits the cryptic conversation between chiron and grover to set up da stakes the movie sorta had it but more importantly doesnt need it as bad they already set up da stakes in the intro is the show cutting it bad well see as it goes on i will say the show is being a lot more subtle about the collusion between chiron and grover i dont know how i feel about that by this point in the movie and the book we know that however much theyre hiding they are on percys side we dont in the show as for the rest of the skeleton following filling in the meat of the section there are a few places where i feel the visualsacting let the show down even if there arent changes on the other hand i think the initial narrated montage was executed well visually but changes the character of percy fundamentally obviously the book being first person means percys narration pulls a ton of heavy lifting characterizationwise that a tv show cant really use the same way logan lermans performance in the movie goes a decent way towards showing that angry darkly sarcastic side of percy walkers performance comes off too calm which is compounded by the writing changes already softening him the sally flashback well see the book used that part for foreshadowing the overarching plot the movie used it for exposition the show seems to be using it to showcase a central theme ill reserve judgement until we see how it works out for them section 3 after yancy before minotaur book percy and grover take the bus back home grover gives percy his card and explains hes percys protector which seems nonsensical to percy bus breaks down leading to the first big scene in this section the fates three old ladies knitting giant blue socks at a fruit stand across the road grover freaks out upon seeing them and even more when percy tells him he saw them cut the string there is a reference to a last time and percy is convinced grover thinks hes going to die this is a big dramatic scene the first time we see proof that the myths are real the setup to grovers character arc i really hope the adaptations do it justice moving on percy ditches grover and heads home we get sallys backstory gabes introhes a giant scumbag and sallys first appearance shes the perfect mom she never raises her voice at anyone its like she always sees the good in percy never the bad yes i am putting this here to attack the show later thank you at this point the movies earlier intros to sally and gabe are holding up decently sally is okay the movie doesnt quite get that warmth you feel through the pages shes just a good mom in a tough situation gabe was done really well in the movie though sally surprises percy with the montauk trip having to appease gabriel to get to go on it also as on odd sidenote grovers warding off evil gesture works on gabe huh at montauk we get the blue food explanation learn more about percys dad and have some nice momson bonding also the start of sallys arc in her explaining why she cant be with him and why she didnt want to send him to camp the section ends with the eagle vs horse dream setting up the central conflict of the book and grover shows up revealing hes a satyr to cap it off movie start 1455 end at 1557 yeah we dont get the fates lame instead we get percy and grover walking to percys home and grover explaining hes percys protector then cut to the house the reveal works but with the movie cutting grover being bullied it doesnt work quite as well and combined with cutting the fates scene we miss out on a big piece of groundwork for grovers arc hes on crutches yes but other than that hes fine thatll be important later on and damit i wanted to see the fates they could have done so much with camera focus sound design to really bring that moment to life okay back at percys place gabes ordering sally around including the skincrawling line cant you see shes servicing me and my friends grover protects percy from gabe and them and sally need to go right now and thats it so a lot of the initial setup of percys home life happened earlier a pretty clever way to show what life is generally like since unlike the book you cant put in backstory paragraphs i dont love cutting the cabin we dont get to see much about how percy and sally care for each other having grover stay with percy is a choice im ambivalent about it makes sense because without the fates scene why would percy ditch him and seeing gabe beat up does feel good but i think itll be a net negative both to grovers characterization and the gabe plotline further on the horse and eagle dream isnt missed here since we got the opening scene instead to serve its purpose no blue food sadness of note this whole section only takes 1 minute show bridge 1210 end 2418 we start off with a nice showing of bad weather in new york its grey its rainy i like it looking back it was perfectly sunny in the movie wheres the bad weather okay in the show and the book the bolt is stolen at the winter solstice but in the movie its only stolen a few weeks before the summer solstice still lame a cut to percy entering his apartment with gabe yelling at the superintendant being heard through the door i guess that means we just aint getting the fates huh and this is a reason why the show had grover betray percy because with them on bad terms percy goes home alone like the book without needing the fates scene to separate them is it worth it eh we also lose the protector reveal eddie the super gets a nice little bit i like that i think it was a good adaptationexpansion of his moment in the book good change there 10 seconds and it sets the scene well we meet gabe hes a jerk but he doesnt come off as a total scumbag yes he answers his wifes cellphone yes hes unpleasant but hes talking to percy about percys expellment and when he hears why we get a closeup of him shrugging and just saying okay and he drops it he tries to lay the law down on percy gets called out for losing at imaginary poker and starts defending himself he even acknowledges that this happens every time with them hes nonthreatening because hes in a recliner with the footrest up and a laptop on his lap the whole time instead of coming off as this overpowering boor like in the book he just seems like a loser boyfriend movie gabe every line hes had makes you want to punch him show gabe so far seems pitiable sallys outside on the fire escape in the rain her meeting percy is done well in the show you can do a lot with just a smile and she does side note walkers finally letting his face show how bad things are for him good on him percy starts to tell her about whats been happening to him and we get the going to montauk part i dont like how this is executed it starts off with sally yelling for gabe she starts declaring whats going to happen and generally comes off as the aggressor in the argument that follows gabe doesnt come off bad or unreasonable here just a bit rude and hotheaded sallys taking his car on short notice he wants the peppers on his sandwich and he wants to watch the game with his wife which they had already planned to do and both enjoy it makes sally come off worse small note i wish percy were more excited to go to montauk in the book it was their yearly thing something he looked forward to something gabe had taken away in the show its like a spur of the moment thing discussed with gabe not percy instead of addressing percys admission he feels scared percys trying to tell his mother something important she changes the subject it doesnt sit right with me we get a dream here with percy being taunted in the rain by a ghost with a lantern uhh im not sure what this adds but maybe itll make sense later ill reserve judgement they get to the cabin and race each other in i really like that that cabin was not looking welcoming with the rain and all but that little moment does a good job of showing that this is their place great moment we get a bit of nice bonding and then on to the big talk that was delayed okay were learning about percys dad now first though we have to get through sally dodging questions twice by redirecting the conversation and talking over percy we get the reveal that percy is a demigod watching this conversation again its a finely acted scene but the characters are wrong this is very similar to the relationship between percy and mr brunner in the book the mentor trying to uplift percy to explain what he needs to know but percys not ready to hear it yet the struggle in sallys voice percys outburst its working but its a scene where percy is being let down by someone he cares for thats a departure from the book sally is presented as a parent who knows whats best rather than a parent who is sacrificing themselves for their kid grover shows up and him and sally talk a bit while percy tries to get an answer about the goat legs its becoming a running thing how sally is driving the plot against percys will im afraid section 4 minotaur book we start hot on the gas literally with sally speeding and grover droppin lore in the car greek myths all real monsters on the hunt destination camp lightning blasts them off the road grover is down and percy is told to get to the tree and dont stop percy refuses to leave grover and sally behind and sally explains to percy how to dodge the minotaurs charge percy reaches the tree sally leads the minotaur away from grover and gets caught percy goes bullfighting to protect grover minotaur hits a tree as percy jumps on top of it breaks the horn slays the minotaur carries grover to the big house and passes out mr brunner and annabeth collect him not a big character scene but its our first big action sequence and we get to see how loyal percy is to his friend also the payoff to sally explaining she was selfish by keeping percy close she paid for it in the end movie car 1602 collapse 2026 its a sunny afternoon on the highway sigh percy asks about camp and it segues into him learning about his dad ayy its like a little bit of the cabin but with grover making snide comments in the backseat also sally answering all of percys questions side note logan lerman is getting a ton of value out of flexing his hand both him and walker have been doing a good job of showing percys inherent anginess during this scene through body language the reveal of percys dad being somethinga god is interrupted by a cow to the road like the lightning bolt but cow car flipped the grover satyr reveal complete with donkey clarification unfortunately grover is not out of it this time around so they make it to camp with plenty of time since they arent carrying grover and also camps in the middle of a forest not on a hill and its an arch not a pine tree i hope that doesnt bode ill for any major story points wink grover and percy make it across sally gets bounced and then snatched by the minotaur as shes telling percy to leave her behind i dont like how the movie takes away sallys moment here helping percy teaching him how to fight percy pulls out his pen and we get the first riptide transformation but the minotaur dont care and backhands him into a tree leading percy to use the broken horn for the kill eh it gets the job done the minotaur doesnt evaporate its just dead by the way percy collapses from exhaustion into grovers arms that is that its a decent fight scene but it misses the character motivations and grover not being knocked out might have some complications later on show car 2424 end credits 3341 grover starts out with some canned new demigod spiel and then we get the exposition about him being a satyr percys protector mrs dodds is real the mist and camp i dont mind the exposition its in the books its a good place to put it sally still isnt answering questions also the minotaur is wearing underpants but we cant really see it he wasnt in the movie but tbh i didnt really care lightning misses and instead the car is totaled by the minotaur locking horns with it and sally spinning out after breaking free grover kicks out the windshield like in the movie but after a slow establishing shot from a cut to black first camp has a hill and a tree this time they stop to talk and for sally to force grover to swear he will protect percy from anything that so much as looks at him funnynot an exaggeration percys questions get ignored some more percy and sally say goodbye and grover reminds them of the minotaur thats been roaring that entire time grover and percy start up the hill while sally takes percys coat to distract the minotaur like percy does in the book she gets dusted percy pulls out riptide in a transformation not quite as good as the movie i like the bronzey glow though percy gets disarmed climbs the minotaur the regular way and sees the halfbroken horn snaps it off and stabs for the kill interestingly i think the book has the weakest horn break the show has it crack from the car then percy finishes the job the movie has the minotaur break it off to get out of a tree in the book percy just snaps it on his own theres a cut to black and percy wakes upsorta with a crowd dispersing and chiron welcoming him to camp theyve been expecting him my problem here is that the show version is fully twice as long as the movie version but unlike section 3 where the show has more scenes is following the book closer its the same scenes the drive and the minotaur fight the show is just taking longer and it loses out on urgency as a result again grover not being knocked out hurts the scene instead of the minotaur catching up because theyre carrying grover he catches up because they stand around talking sally gets to have more of a moment here albeit via heroic sacrifice id like it but it doesnt feel like it accomplishes anything percy essentially walks in a circle in the time sallys distracting the minotaur this goes for the movie too but again the show misses out the percy protecting his friend angle and it weakens his motivation a little the fight was solid but it didnt need the standing around talking conclusion so far i think the movie is adapting the book better it has the advantage of tlts opening having a lot of opportunities to nondirectly adapt stuff so having only 23 the runtime doesnt affect it as much trimming scenes is easy with the early exposition heavy starting chapters you can work in the exposition somewhere else as opposed to missing key character development the show has a few scenes the book cuts but it doesnt capitalize on it well with mischaracterizations ending up dragging the show down past the movies weak characterizations movie gabe vs show gabe is a slaughter on all fronts but show sallys habit of not answering questions puts her behind movie sally whos just kind of there also the show tries to build up da stakes through dialogue at several different times but its too vague we havent got any hints of the main plot yet we keep hearing that percy is important but we dont know why meanwhile the book has already started peppering in the seeds via the eavesdropping and the dream and the movie decided subtlety is overrated and had its opening its just my opinion but i think the going bold worked

lil chapter 78 brynjolf a handsome in a fittingly roguish kind of way nord and i slip out of riften exiting it by walking out of gates located near the hold capitals palace a pristine vista of what trying to create empathy in a game taught us about making games and about people post published first in rgamedev on november 2025 our studios direction can be described along two axes exploring the possibilities opened up by creating nonviolent games making games where the design itself is the vehicle of the message we want to express i explain this below we believe that what makes video games distinct from other media is the interaction between human and software the deepest messages are conveyed by how one plays not just what one reads or hears when playing in short the main message of the game is carried first by the system and then by the narrative our first game fireside feelings came out of a corollary question this post tells how we attempted to answer that what we failed at what we found and what we learnt about creation and about listening people we are team empreintes a small horizontallystructured team based in angoulme in the southwest of france in practice there are two of us jaximus and me vidu we do everything together sometimes awkwardly often passionately we began developing games around 2020 and in june 2025 during the wholesome direct we released our first official game fireside feelings today we are working on our second project the granny detective society fireside feelings is an asynchronous conversational game the principle is simple you pick a topic you create your character you sit by a fire with another player and respond but the discussion is not in real time when you see the other players answer it is actually that players answer from their playthrough when they answered the question themselves this timeoffset is in part the key to the game just the time to think and to be sincere but it took us a long way to arrive here at the start we began with this idea so how can we create a framework that favours the emergence of empathy so we experimented a lot first we wanted to eliminate all form of performance we wanted to clarify the frame so it was obvious you were there for two things 1 to deposit yourself share your thoughts your emotions after reflection 2 to receive listen to what someone else has deposited before you without judging without arguing when you read someones testimony that person will never know they shared it with you you are alone facing a small piece of humanity sincere and fragile and all we ask is that you welcome it then we worked on total anonymity at first the pseudonyms remained visible and some people recognised each other that broke the magic the sense of intimacy the safe place so we anonymised absolutely everything including the avatar design to avoid players posting images of the characters to find their owners also our players embody anthropomorphic animals to neutralise physical or social assumptions while preserving expressive warmth we wanted the characters to give an emotional colour rather than a social origin we also added trigger warnings not to censor but to allow everyone to navigate between sensitivities without being exposed to painful narratives finally we blocked the possibility to modify ones answer after reading another players its a small detail but it changes everything you write what you feel not what you think you should say you dont react you express and above all we insisted on being totally transparent this is not a chat nor an ai its a human exchange system giving and receiving and this is told to the player as soon as they arrive in the game and several times during their experience what we hadnt anticipated however was how contagious sincerity can be in the game all answers are handmoderated and what we learnt to look for in our moderation were messages that were sincere affirmed intimate because we observed that sincerity is contagious indeed for every new player confronted with an entry thus moderated we observed roughly the same phenomenon initially responses are short shy then message after message they lengthen deepen become personal and thus become highquality responses even at a festival in the noise standing up surrounded we saw players pause breathe and write moving texts that is when we said to ourselves damn this is so cool the set up works the context dictates the behaviour one of our big early project blind spots was that we hadnt thought our frame through properly at first we tried to imitate a classic discussion a character asked a question responded triggered another but everything felt fake two things were missing an anchor point from one discussion to the next a moderator to put players on equal footing one day as we had written to mathew of wholesome games to introduce our game he told us a key phrase and everything clicked we created spark a small flame that lives in each campfire spark doesnt judge doesnt debate it listens links voices gives rhythm it became the heart of the game from there everything opened up one of our objectives was thus to create a space favouring wellbeing in both senses of the word acting well and feeling well our first reflex was to reward kindness to create an external motivation pushing toward benevolence so we added a gift system little shooting stars you could give to a player whose answer you liked on paper it was seductive but very quickly people began writing to receive gifts and sincerity disappeared we discussed this with ziba of popcannibal kind words who told us that phrase served as our compass we needed instead to remove all form of competition all form of performance race all form of external motivation to let the player develop internal motivations stronger and healthier i wont go into the details of the moderation system here maybe in another post if people are interested but you should know that all responses are read and handmoderated by two persons we wanted to avoid becoming slaves to our own game while keeping a human link in the process but overall we were extremely surprised at how much players grasped wholeheartedly and spontaneously the idea of selfmoderating their content let me explain when you finish a conversation you can take a polaroid photo then all your polaroids are pasted above your bed and you can reread your conversations and when you click on a polaroid you can assign a triggerwarning to your conversation its quite badly thought and tedious honestly we didnt really count on it but regardless we realised that a large majority of players themselves filled in their own trigger warnings without any external motivation people took care of one another small aside from a more personal point of view having read hundreds of messages we understood something simple and immense to be listened to understood loved for the people they care about to be happy and healthy our common values are far closer than what social networks and the press let us believe it might seem a little nave but its an idea that has deeply marked me yes and no the launch was a bit chaotic our publisher chose a shadow drop of the game without a real marketing campaign before during or after before the launch we had barely 2000 wishlists but thanks to the wholesome direct the community took over and the reception was overwhelming players wrote to us that it was the game of their life others thanked us for having made the internet softer if only for a moment a journalist told us she only had one thing to look forward to each evening entering the games bubble of softness we also saw an unexpected echo from the furry and vtubing communities i spent hours chatting with members of these communities on discord and i discovered there a kindness and depth i hadnt imagined today fireside feelings is 6700 sales 23000 wishlists entirely organic 97 positive reviews on steam its not the game that will make us financially safe but its so much more than that the framework creates the behaviour if you want kindness design for it transparency creates trust the clearer you are the freer people feel performance and competition carry a form of violence they can have their place but only if they are chosen deliberately and above all its the first time in our lives as artists that we release a project and simply feel proud of its impact even if some parts of the game are awkward even if some drawings make us wince we know we will never be ashamed of having made this game and thats a fabulous feeling thank you for reading all the way if the topic interests you i could write another post about sustainable human moderation by two people and if youd like to discuss it it would be with great pleasure

what can we learn by watching people learn how observing learners becomes a shortcut to understanding ourselves framing the question when we start watching people learnreally watchingwe discover that every classroom meeting room and zoom call is a live documentary about how humans change instead of only asking what did they learn we can ask how did they get there and suddenly patterns appear how people handle confusion seek help use feedback and bounce back from mistakes this lens turns everyday scenestraining sessions first days on the job someone learning a new appinto data about motivation mindset and culture why this matters by studying how people learn we gain a practical playbook for building better teams designing clearer training and improving our own learning habits the question isnt just academic its a daily leadership parenting and selfdevelopment tool learning as a mirror watching someone else learn is like holding up a mirror to our own habitsonly the reflection is less defended and more honest some people lean forward ask questions early and take messy notes others hang back silently test their understanding and only speak when theyre sure a few jump in fail publicly and laugh it off each style is a live demonstration of how safe they feel to be wrong what they believe about their own ability how they think serious adults are supposed to behave when we notice these patterns we cant help but ask which of these do i do the act of watching people learn becomes a subtle selfaudit it shows us where we rush where we avoid and where we lock up to protect our image instead of our growth what you see when you watch people learn if you zoom in on any learning momentsomeone tackling a new tool a colleague presenting for the first time a friend trying a new sportyoull often spot the same recurring moves framing the challenge do they see it as a test dont screw this up or a playground lets see what happens managing confusion do they freeze fake competence ask for help or experiment on their own using feedback do they treat feedback as threat validation or raw material to improve regulating emotion do they spiral from one mistake or treat it as data and keep going adults rarely narrate these steps out loud but their behavior shouts them by paying attention you start to see that smart often just means good at cycling quickly through try notice adjust try again that pattern is universalfrom apprenticeships to executive coaching a realworld example the onboarding observer picture a manager quietly watching three new hires during a product onboarding session one keeps asking naive questions early even when others stay silent another takes meticulous notes but rarely talks then sends sharp followup questions afterward the third clicks around in the software during the demo breaks something and laughs while fixing it from this the manager can learn more than any personality test might reveal who is comfortable exposing gaps in real time who prefers private processing before speaking who learns best by doing even at the risk of visible mistakes now the manager can design support that fits offer office hours and written guides for the quiet notetaker encourage the questionasker to help shape faqs and onboarding materials give the experimenter sandbox environments where breaking things is safe and encouraged by watching people learn the manager doesnt just judge performancethey understand learning patterns which are far more useful for longterm growth turning everyday moments into a learning lab you dont need a formal study daily life is full of chances to turn observation into insight try this in your next meeting workshop or mentoring session name the learning moves you see you tried three different ways to explain that conceptthats iteration you paused to ask if you were on trackthats seeking early feedback notice the environment does the room or culture reward questions or eyeroll them do people speak up only after leaders speak or before the context often explains the learning behavior watch for turning points when someone hits a wall what happens next do they double down alone invite help or quietly disengage that moment is a goldmine for understanding motivation and safety reflect it back on yourself ask when i learn something hard which of those moves do i default to which do i avoid now your observation has turned into a mirror counterpoint its possible to overromanticize peoples natural learning styles some of us do better with controlled theorydriven approaches the real opportunity is to blend what we observe with evidence from cognitive sciencespacing retrieval deliberate practiceso our admiration becomes design not just inspiration bringing it together and putting it to work what can we learn by watching people learn quite a lot how psychological safety really feels in a room how individuals relate to mistakes and uncertainty how culture either amplifies or shuts down curiosity most importantly we see that learning is less about inborn talent and more about structures beliefs and behavior loops once you can spot those loops in others you can redesign your own ask one more question make one more attempt request one more piece of feedback if you want to train your eye for this try treating your next class training or team meeting as a mini field studytake notes not just on the content but on the learning behavior in the room and if this kind of question helps you see the world differently follow questionclasss questionaday at questionclasscoma simple daily prompt to sharpen how you notice think and learn bookmarked for you to go deeper on observing and shaping how people learn the art of learning by josh waitzkin a firstperson look at mastery that reveals how patterns of focus feedback and emotion shape performance make it stick the science of successful learning by peter c brown henry l roediger iii and mark a mcdaniel a researchbacked tour of what actually helps people remember and apply what they learn helping people change by richard boyatzis melvin smith and ellen van oosten explores coaching conversations that tap into peoples motivations not just their todo lists questionstrings to practice questionstrings are deliberately ordered sequences of questions in which each answer fuels the next creating a compounding ladder of insight that drives progressively deeper understanding what to do now use this string after you observe someone learningthen apply the same questions to your own behavior or your teams culture learningpattern string for turning casual observation into practical change what did they actually do when they didnt understand what did that say about how safe they felt to be confused what kind of support or structure would have helped them take a better next step how does our environment encourage or discourage that better step what one small change could i maketodayto model or design healthier learning behavior try weaving this into debriefs after workshops 11s or even your own journaling it trains you to see learning as a system you can shape not a mystery you just endure in the end watching people learn is less about judging their abilities and more about decoding the conditions beliefs and habits that make growth possiblefor them and for you

potw 137 schubert string quartet no15 in g major good morning everyone happy monday and welcome back to another season of our subs listening club each week well listen to a piece recommended by the community discuss it learn about it and hopefully introduce us to music we wouldnt hear otherwise last time we met we listened to rossinis william tell overture you can go back to listen read up and discuss the work if you want to our next piece of the week is franz schuberts string quartet no15 in g major d887 1826 score from imslp some listening notes from mark steinberg borges writes in his poem adam is your ashes all things are their own prophecy of dust iron is rust the voice already echo the fluid duality which suffuses our experience of the world joy that melts into sorrow and sorrow that is tinged with hope is at the very core of schuberts music his experience of time can be more painterly than narrative all is present simultaneously and we need to approach his works with a patience that allows us to grasp his yearning toward acceptance rather than resolution we have one important prose document from franz schubert a brief personal essay entitled my dream whether or not it represents an accurate depiction of an actual dream it seems to sum up much of the emotional essence of his music in it he writes for long years i felt torn between the greatest grief and the greatest lovewhenever i attempted to sing of love it turned to pain and again when i tried to sing of pain it turned to love thus were love and pain divided in me for schubert there is no false hope of banishing the one and holding on to the other not only do love and pain coexist in his soul but he recognizes that they are one and the same the one contained in and giving meaning to the other the opening of the g major string quartet is a case in point the opening major chords erupt into minor this is not a tragic proclamation or harbinger of doom but rather an exploration of and an opening of space within the hanging major chords a recognition of what poet mark doty calls no hope without the possibility of a wound even though the gesture is forceful and vehement a sense of instability and vulnerability underlies it and in fact the continuation of the movement brings us to a tremulous place where we can gaze into the uncertainty and begin to look for a way to hold major and minor close and allow them to occupy the same space without vying for exclusive claim on truth this modal oscillation characterizes each movement of the work from the dramatic juxtapositions of the opening movement through the wanderings and eruptions of the second into the scherzo with its magical evocation of far off contentment in its trio to the finale where schubert dances between major and minor and turns to nearly every key bringing more and more of our experience into the circle of acceptance to appreciate schuberts way of organizing time in general and certainly in this piece one must understand his priorities it may be of use to contrast his trajectory through a piece with beethovens which for most people is a more immediately satisfying path one of the things we so cherish about beethoven is that he admits the full range of human experience and then transcends whatever obstacles he encounters his is a vision of music as narrative as a journey toward resolution and a demonstration of the strength of the human spirit we understand beethoven because he recognizes so much of our experience of the world and then tells us that we can survive in that world and find our rightful place solidly within it schubert has no such certainty nor does he attempt to find it hindu deities have multiple forms peaceful as well as wrathful and all are admitted as parts of their divinity schubert is like that opening up more and more to the beauty of experience whether or not that experience is beautiful as we commonly understand it his music helps us see the totality of who we are and contain it all without working toward closure and completion one of the important concepts in carl jungs vision of the human psyche is the existence of the shadow those aspects of ourselves from which we turn away and which need to be reintegrated into our personalities if we are to remain whole and fully ourselves a work such as schuberts g major quartet addresses shadow qualities exploring them and admitting them into the light for anyone who will allow herself or himself to be transported into its world this quartet will offer manifold revelations there are moments in each movement which seem especially to encapsulate particular truths which are important to schubert the recapitulation or return to the opening material in the first movement is extraordinary in that the sense of return is strong and unmistakable and yet nothing is the same the startling dynamic contrasts are gone the jagged rhythms are smoothed out instead of shuddering tremolos we have rolling triplets that seem gently to console and yet with all of this contrast the sense is not that there were conflicts that have been resolved but rather that what we are hearing was there all along had we chosen to understand it in that way we should have no expectation that the more difficult opening idea has been banished but only that we see how to admit it into our experience without being completely overwhelmed the wanderer in the second movement twice encounters a storm in the midst of its fury as the music searches for a way out a defiant twonote rising figure in the first violin and viola not coincidentally the inversion of the falling third that comes again and again in the previous movement tenaciously recurs oblivious to the shifting modulations surrounding it it becomes more and more foreign to its environment what is extraordinary is that there is no attempt to integrate it into the fabric of the ongoing progress of the music it is left there unresolved and unresolvable yet the movement ends in peace without having conquered it there is a way to go on through recognition rather than victory sometimes it happens that performers do their best freest playing in encores the pressure of the concert proper is past and there is a sense of easygoing possibility and sometimes composers write some of their most touching free music in the middle trio sections of minuet or scherzo movements untethered from the more rigorous formal constraints in other movements the trio of the scherzo of this quartet is surely one of those cases where music that is framed by a restless shuddering movement can for a brief moment revel in the vision of another world one liberated from earthly concerns later in schuberts dream he writes and one day i had news of a gentle maiden who had just died and a circle formed around her grave in which many youths and old men walked as though in everlasting bliss they spoke softly so as not to wake the maiden heavenly thoughts seemed forever to be showered on the youths from the maidens gravestone like fine sparks producing a gentle rustling i too longed sorely to walk there only a miracle however can lead you to that circle they said but i went to the gravestone with slow steps and lowered gaze filled with devotion and firm belief and before i was aware of it i found myself in the circle which uttered a wondrously lovely sound and i felt as though eternal bliss were gathered together into a single moment this trio is such a moment of course it is not a place we can stay as we see upon the return of the movement proper yet even though it is a peace and a bliss which is brought to us through the release of death it becomes a part of who we are and what we can know in the same family of movements as the tarantellalike finales of the d minor quartet and the c minor piano sonata this last movement has the energy of a night ride on horseback through open terrain a recurrent passage has the whole quartet moving together in gasps reaching for something unknown the terrible revelation it seems to be reaching toward is unrevealed always answered by an almost naive sounding dance the passage is extended each time it appears until its final statement has a nearly unbearable intensity the chasm opens before us as we go barreling through from key to key waiting for a landing of some sort and eventually we land through all our wanderings back in the key where we started our journey having seen everything around it and able to live where we are with a feeling of acceptance and hope that hope is as vaclav havel defines it in disturbing the peace hope is definitely not the same thing as optimism it is not a conviction that something will turn out well but the certainty that something makes sense regardless of how it doors of dimensia a depth crawl adventure compatible with fabula ultima doors of dimensia was originally conceived as a dungeon generator that didnt require the rigorous attention paid to the dungeons layout ironically when i discovered that i was essentially trying to reinvent the depth crawl dod became the opposite of its original design goal this came from playing a lot of games that disregarded the resource management of fantasy roleplaying games which automatically took place in a dungeon for example i was quite surprised with fabula ultimas rules on dungeons on the one hand i really liked the games standard flow of moving back and forth between conflict scenes and interlude scenes but i still wanted the feel of an adventure inside of a dungeon after all the video games i played in my youth that were formative to me are also formative to fabula ultima this is where putting a depth crawl to fabula ultima resolves this tension at my table my players love it a depth crawl is not a dungeon crawl they are similar in tone but diverge in method of play in a classic dungeon crawl minute discrete details of the player characters surroundings are paramount the circumstances inform play from aspects that seem as innocuous as the angle of the floor to the furnishing of rooms all the way up to the shape of the dungeon itself at large in a depth crawl space can be far more ambiguous and illusive this is a feature it is not a bug for the purpose of dimensia depth is an abstraction of how far the player characters have progressed into the adventure what really matters is that the gm and the players keep track of the order of what was experienced when the player characters want to progress in the dungeon they simply do you add one depth roll a new location on the depth crawl chart with the appropriate dice and add the current depth to that score many locations in dimensia arent assumed to be dangerous like in a standard dungeon crawl theyre just weird lol and have lots of strange technologies magics and npcs to discover this style of adventure perfectly rhymes with the natural cadence of what fabula ultima wants to achieve when its player characters are in a dangerous location doors of dimensia represents my attempt to reframe dungeon adventures as something different from tenfoot pole economics it was mainly play tested with fabula ultima troika and some other osr style games it has broadly appliable conversion rules but it has preformed best for me with fabula ultima if any of that sounds interesting to you please consider following the project and backing it when it goes live this upcoming sunday zimo is upon us and there are tons of cool new projects trying to get off the ground

an overview of the ruvector world model ruvector is not a text predictor it is a structural world model heres how it works it represents reality as a living system composed of vectors graphs constraints and signals the objective is not to guess the next token the objective is to maintain an internally coherent model as the world changes over time think less chatbot think control system with memory core primitives vectors vectors encode meaning as position they represent state intent observations memory and outcomes in a shared geometric space similar concepts cluster together but distance matters because it directly feeds reasoning attention and control decisions graphs graphs encode structure nodes represent entities actions rules and constraints edges represent relationships such as causality dependency and enforcement the graph is dynamic relationships evolve as new evidence arrives attention attention is not relevance scoring it is routing ruvector attention controls where computation flows across the vector graph based on current state uncertainty and risk it decides what matters now not what sounds plausible dynamic minimum cut this is the defining mechanism minimum cut continuously measures structural tension inside the graph when different regions of the model disagree energy rises that tension becomes signal disagreement is not failure disagreement is information how the world model runs signals are ingested from tools sensors agents users or simulations they are embedded into vector space and linked into the graph coherence is evaluated using cuts flows and energy actions are gated based on structural health learning occurs locally and incrementally when coherence stabilizes the system returns to a quiet baseline no constant chatter no hallucinated confidence why this matters large language models optimize for plausibility at a moment in time ruvector optimizes for stability under change instead of asking is this answer correct the system asks is this world still intact that shift enables long running agents offline operation self correction and explainable decisions bottom line ruvector treats intelligence as continuous structural maintenance rather than episodic prediction optimization converges coherence persists npx ruvector github

the psychology of modern feminism what went wrong and how to find your way back this isnt coming from some antifeminist place i genuinely believe in equality and women having full autonomy over their lives but when i look around at what gets labeled feminist today versus what actually improves womens mental health confidence and quality of life theres a massive disconnect the research backs this up too studies show that despite decades of feminist progress young women report higher rates of anxiety and depression than ever before somethings not adding up ive spent way too many hours down the feminism rabbit hole books podcasts academic papers twitter discourse and honestly something feels off like we took a wrong turn somewhere and now were arguing about stuff that has nothing to do with helping actual women live better lives so i dug deeper read everything from bell hooks to camille paglia listened to debates between different feminist schools of thought and what i found is that the most useful insights about womens wellbeing often come from outside mainstream feminist discourse entirely heres what actually helped 1 the biology denial problem is making women miserable modern feminism often treats biological sex differences as either nonexistent or oppressive social constructs but denying biology doesnt liberate anyone it just leaves women confused about why they feel the way they do dr louann brizendines the female brain breaks down the neurological differences between men and women in a way thats both scientifically rigorous and deeply validating brizendine is a neuropsychiatrist at ucsf and this book won awards for making neuroscience accessible reading it felt like someone finally gave me permission to acknowledge that my hormonal cycle affects my mood energy and social needs and that this isnt weakness or internalized misogyny its just biology the book explains why women are generally more attuned to emotional nuances why we tend to ruminate more and why certain phases of our cycle make us want connection versus solitude this is the best womens neuroscience book ive ever read understanding these patterns helped me work with my biology instead of fighting it 2 the victimhood narrative strips away your agency heres something uncomfortable a lot of modern feminist discourse frames women as perpetual victims who need protection from an endless list of microaggressions and triggers this might feel validating at the moment but research shows that adopting a victim mindset actually increases anxiety and depression while decreasing resilience carol dwecks work on mindset theory demonstrates that people who view challenges as threats rather than opportunities show worse outcomes across basically every life domain the feminist emphasis on cataloging all the ways women are oppressed can inadvertently train women to see themselves as powerless i started using an app called finch for habit building which focuses on small daily actions you can control its a self care app disguised as a cute bird game but what it actually does is retrain your brain to focus on agency rather than victimhood youre not drowning in systemic oppression youre completing small tasks that build confidence that shift in framing makes a massive difference 3 the oversocialization trap nobody talks about women are socialized to be hyperaware of others feelings to accommodate to smooth over conflict to make everyone comfortable mainstream feminism recognizes this but often responds by encouraging women to be more assertive without addressing the deep psychological patterns underneath psychologist martha becks the way of integrity beck worked at harvard and has been oprahs life coach for years tackles this differently she argues that womens biggest problem isnt external oppression its internal selfbetrayal weve been trained to ignore our own knowledge in favor of what others expect this book will make you question everything you think you know about being a good woman beck provides a framework for identifying when youre lying to yourself why its destroying your mental health and how to realign with your actual values rather than performing values you think you should have the chapter on the dark wood of error where she describes the psychological breakdown that comes from prolonged selfbetrayal hit me like a truck if you want a more structured way to work through these patterns theres an app called befreed that pulls from psychology research expert insights and books like the ones mentioned here to create personalized learning plans you can set a specific goal like stop peoplepleasing while staying authentic and it generates audio content tailored to your situation you can adjust the depth from quick 10minute overviews to 40minute deep dives with examples and customize the voice to whatever keeps you engaged it also has a virtual coach you can chat with about your specific struggles which helps translate these concepts into your actual life instead of just absorbing theory 4 real empowerment requires difficult conversations about tradeoffs one thing that frustrates me about mainstream feminism is the you can have it all messaging career relationship kids hobbies social life perfect body all while being politically active and maintaining your mental health its exhausting and its a lie nobody can optimize every life domain simultaneously research on work life balance consistently shows that high achievement in one area typically requires sacrifice in others but admitting this feels taboo in feminist spaces because it sounds like youre saying women should give up their ambitions the life worth podcast by megan fenyoe does an incredible job exploring these tradeoffs honestly she interviews women across different life stages about the choices they made what they gained what they sacrificed and whether theyd do it differently no instagram perfect narratives just real talk about the fact that choosing career advancement might mean less time with your kids or choosing to prioritize family might mean slower professional growth both are valid neither is a feminist failure 5 the comparison trap amplified by social media feminism feminist instagram and tiktok often feel like performance art who can signal the most progressive views whos the most intersectional who can call out problematic behavior most eloquently it turns activism into a competitive sport where women judge each other constantly research from jonathan haidt and jean twenge shows that social media use correlates strongly with increased anxiety and depression in young women specifically the constant social comparison and outrage cycles are poison for mental health i started using insight timer which is a meditation app but also has talks and courses on topics like reducing social media dependence and building genuine selfworth independent of external validation the course unfck your brain by faith harper shes a therapist and sexologist breaks down how our brains get hijacked by social media dopamine loops and provides practical rewiring strategies insanely good resource if you find yourself doom scrolling feminist discourse for hours 6 the missing conversation about female sexuality and desire mainstream feminism talks a lot about consent and assault prevention which is obviously crucial but theres way less discussion about female pleasure desire and sexual agency in a proactive rather than reactive sense emily nagoskis come as you are changed how i understand my own sexuality nagoski has a phd in health behavior and this book is based on actual sex research rather than pop psychology she explains the dual control model of sexual response why spontaneous desire isnt the only normal kind how context affects arousal and why the things that turn you on might be totally different from what turns your partner on this is the best book on female sexuality ive ever encountered its feminist in the sense that it centers womens actual experiences rather than assuming male sexuality is the default but its not preachy or political its just incredibly useful information that somehow doesnt get taught anywhere 7 building real resilience means embracing discomfort modern feminist spaces often emphasize safety comfort and protection from anything that might cause distress but psychological research shows that exposure to manageable challenges is exactly what builds resilience trying to eliminate all discomfort actually makes people more fragile kristin neffs work on selfcompassion offers a better framework she distinguishes between selfesteem which requires feeling superior to others and selfcompassion which acknowledges struggle as part of being human her research shows that selfcompassion is more predictive of wellbeing and resilience than selfesteem the thing is building selfcompassion requires sitting with discomfort rather than immediately seeking validation or filing everything under trauma it means treating yourself with kindness while also pushing yourself to grow that balance gets lost when feminist discourse frames every challenge as oppression 8 the success metrics problem a lot of feminist messaging implicitly assumes that success means achieving in maledominated spaces breaking the glass ceiling becoming a ceo entering stem fields these are valuable goals but theyre not universal measures of a good life plenty of women find deep fulfillment in traditionally feminine pursuits like caregiving teaching creative arts community building feminism should expand options not create a new hierarchy where only certain choices count as empowered the on being podcast with krista tippett explores this beautifully she interviews people across different fields about meaning purpose and what constitutes a life well lived the episode with poet mary oliver titled listening to the world captures something important about defining success on your own terms rather than according to any ideological framework including feminism at the end of the day the point of feminism should be helping women live fuller freer more authentic lives if the discourse isnt doing that for you if its making you more anxious and less capable then somethings broken youre allowed to take whats useful and leave the rest youre allowed to prioritize your actual wellbeing over ideological purity the women i know who seem most genuinely content arent the ones most steeped in feminist theory theyre the ones who figured out what they actually want built lives around those values developed real skills and resilience and stopped performing for an imaginary audience thats the kind of liberation worth pursuing

moving beyond extremes they embody a constant cycle of presence and disappearance a predictable revolving door that ive grown accustomed to i anticipate the return expect the departure while the pattern used to wear me down the emotional impact has finally flatlined people arent vibestheyre a syllabus written in disappearing ink a curriculum of chaos that promises knowledge but delivers only repetition i was trapped in a burning building but the person holding the fire extinguisher was also the one holding the match they set the fire watched me choke on the smoke then put out just enough flame to be called a hero i wasnt being saved i was being kept in the fire a controlled burn designed for my perpetual presence and someone who controls both the damage and the relief isnt helping you escapetheyre making sure you never leave stasis isnt a state where movement ceases rather its the persistent loop of a flawed formula this formula manifests as a dangerous mesmerizing spectacle imagine a steering wheel snapped in two with each piece desperately fighting for control certain its fractured grip can somehow prevent the vehicle from plunging over the cliff its already heading toward repetition is exasperating its patterns behaviors and arguments are so predictable and yet they fill entire librarieslibraries built on the same circular logic but if the core ideas remain the same what makes their cumulative presence meaningful i came to understand that the true geography of consequence isnt mapped by extremes the spectacle the drama the stark oppositiontheyre merely elaborate diversions props on a stage meant to occupy attention while the underlying mechanisms operate unseen like the silent intricate gearing of a clock the actual movement the power that shapes reality resides not in the poles themselves but in the subtle highpressure space connecting them it exists in the narrow pressurized passage that holds all potential for both conflict and resolutionthe untouched liminal boundary beyond the reach of polar opposites where true leverage is found i began to understand that lifes equations are not solved by choosing sidestheyre transcended by locating the hidden axis the direction the spectacle cant account for the silent dimension and in that space the predictable libraries of repetition dissolve they no longer dictate the rhythm of thought or action they merely echo harmlessly in the background like static on an unlistenedto frequency this subtle often invisible space is where real consequence livesthe corridor where tension accumulates where momentum is born where the overlooked force quietly shapes outcomes extremes are spectacle drama is distraction the middle the liminal the pressurized nothingness between the polesthat is where the universe actually moves in that corridorthe narrow pressurized spacei realized that the familiar axes of choice are illusions convenient constructs reality and illusion equilibrium and ascent valley and peak fate and freedom theyre presented as opposites but the opposition exists only in the convenience of perception the lazy minds need for neat boxes the universe doesnt pledge allegiance to either side it moves along the path of least resistance because that is the easiest story to tell the simplest simulation to maintain the one that guarantees repetition the path of least resistance is seductive it lulls you into comfort into repetition into the false security of predictability i had called it fate but fate is merely inertiathe inertial footprint of thought left unexamined the accumulated weight of unoriginal choices the true frontier does not lie on the familiar horizon it lies along the unchosen axis the direction no one dares explore because it violates the logic of extremes the cardinal rule of the controlled drama and there it was the missing particle not a particle at allbut an escape vector a rotational shift the asterisk in the equation that rendered the spectacle irrelevant once truly seen paradox doesnt need solving it dissolves losing its power to bind equilibrium is no longer a goalit is the trap the comfortable floor of the burning building the poles themselves the screeching extremes are artifacts convenient illusions that only exist for minds convinced in their twodimensional map of a multidimensional reality the force i sought wasnt originit was freedom freedom from the axes altogether freedom to rotate out of the plane where causes compete where the choice is always fixed truth isnt found on one side waiting to be selected it is the dimension through which selection becomes unnecessary the space where the duality implodes in that space paradox bucklednot from conflict but from sheer irrelevance duality collapsed the choice between extremes evaporated i didnt choose a side i stepped into the axis where choosing no longer matters the zeropoint of the entire system paradox became irrelevant equilibrium revealed itself as an illusion truth became the function that destroys its own boundaries expanding the limits of what is possible what remained was not a destination but navigationa map drawn as you walk it a universe that reveals its frontier only to those willing to abandon the worn path to defy the gravitational pull of the familiar the dance continuesnot from paradox nor from equilibrium but from the only force that transcends both the will to move in a direction the universe has not yet imagined the vector of pure unconstrained creation this wasnt an idea i adopted it was a movement i felt the first time my choices stopped echoing and started diverging
